claim: Patreon's paid-creator population contracted for the first time in its recorded history, falling from a peak of 295,083 creators in October 2025 to 286,287 in February 2026 — a roughly 3% decline in four months, described by the source as about 5% down since June 2025 — after nine straight years of monotonic growth.
stance_target: The claim that net creator attrition is now measurable at platform scale and can exceed new entry
scope_conditions: Census-style scrape of public Patreon pages by Graphtreon, not a survey; population defined as creators with at least one PAYING member, so it excludes creators with only free members and cannot distinguish creators who quit from creators who merely lost their last paying patron; no country breakdown — Patreon is US-headquartered and its creator base is undisclosed by geography; figures are point-in-time snapshots roughly every six months
quoted_support: Based on Graphtreon data, 286,287 creators have at least one paying member as of February 2026. That's a drop of around 5% since June 2025.
region: Global platform, US-headquartered, no country breakdown

claim: Total monthly Patreon creator payouts have been essentially flat at roughly $24 million since January 2022 while the paid-creator population grew from 172,176 to 286,287 over the same period, meaning average visible earnings per paid creator fell from about $140/month to about $84/month — a roughly 40% decline in four years.
stance_target: The claim that creator earnings per head are declining as entry outpaces the growth of total money available to creators
scope_conditions: IMPORTANT SCOPE MISMATCH: the Graphtreon payout figure explicitly EXCLUDES creators with hidden earnings, so it is a visible-earnings subtotal, while the creator count includes all creators with a paying member — the resulting per-creator levels are therefore lower bounds, not true means. The trend remains informative only if the hidden-earnings share is stable over time, which is not verified. Patreon's own disclosure of over $2 billion in annual creator earnings for 2025 implies roughly $167M/month, about 7x the Graphtreon visible figure. Derived by the analyst from the source's two tables, not stated in the source.
quoted_support: Creators on Patreon earned a total of $23.97 million (excluding creators with hidden earnings; actual earnings may vary significantly) in January 2026. Monthly payouts have dropped 0.72% over the last year, down from $24.14 million in January 2025.

claim: Using Patreon's own disclosed figures, mean annual earnings per paid creator are approximately $6,990 (over $2 billion annually divided among 286,287 creators with a paying member), or about $582/month — a mean that on a documented power-law distribution sits far above the median creator.
stance_target: The claim that mean creator earnings substantially overstate typical creator earnings on membership platforms
scope_conditions: Derived by the analyst by combining Patreon's company-disclosed 2025 annual creator earnings with the Graphtreon February 2026 creator count — two different sources and slightly different dates; company earnings figures are self-reported and unaudited (Patreon is private and 'doesn't regularly disclose financial information'); the figure is gross of Patreon's 5-12% platform cut and payment processing fees; no median is published by either source
quoted_support: According to a 2025 company update, creators on Patreon earn over $2 billion annually on the platform. Overall, creator earnings on the platform have increased by 150% since 2020.

claim: Patronage on Patreon is extremely concentrated: only 31 creators out of 286,287 — approximately 0.011%, or about 1 in 9,200 — have more than 20,000 paying members each.
stance_target: The claim that creator success is a winner-take-most distribution in which the top tier is a vanishingly small fraction of participants
scope_conditions: Measured by Graphtreon scrape of public Patreon pages, current as of the February 2026 page update; counts paying members not earnings, and members-per-creator is an imperfect earnings proxy since per-member pledge amounts vary widely (the top creator by members, Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast with 124,452 members, does not disclose earnings, while Chapo Trap House with 46,218 members shows $198,278/month); the 0.011% figure is derived by the analyst
quoted_support: Currently, only 31 creators on Patreon receive sponsorship from more than 20,000 paying members each. The top creator (ranked by number of paid members) on Patreon is Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast, a comedy podcast; 124,452 paid members sponsor the show.

claim: Patreon creator growth decelerated sharply and then reversed: the platform added roughly 20,000 paid creators per six-month period from 2017 to 2023, but lost about 8,800 between October 2025 and February 2026.
stance_target: The claim that the creator economy's participant base has stopped expanding on at least one major direct-monetization platform
scope_conditions: Derived from the source's Graphtreon time series; snapshot intervals are irregular (Feb/Aug through 2024, then November 2024, October 2025, February 2026), so period-over-period rates are not strictly comparable; the count measures creators with at least one paying member, a threshold that conflates market exit with loss of the final patron

claim: Patreon takes 5% to 12% of creator earnings plus payment processing fees depending on plan tier, so gross creator earnings figures overstate creator take-home by roughly a tenth before tax.
stance_target: The claim that headline creator earnings figures are gross of platform fees
scope_conditions: Platform fee schedule as of 2026; the range depends on which product plan a creator selects; payment processing is additional and unquantified here; comparison point for other platforms in this corpus (OnlyFans 20%, YouTube 45%, Twitch 50%)
quoted_support: Patreon makes money by taking a cut of all creator earnings generated through the platform. Patreon currently takes between 5% and 12% of creator earnings (plus a payment processing fee), depending on the product plan.

claim: Patreon's audience base has also plateaued, holding at 10 million monthly active paying members from 2024 through 2025 after adding roughly 1 million per year from 2017 to 2024, against more than 60 million free memberships.
stance_target: The claim that the demand side of direct creator monetization has stopped growing, capping total creator income
scope_conditions: Company-reported figures compiled from Patreon newsroom posts, Fast Company and TechCrunch; the 2025 entry is given imprecisely as '10 million+'; the free-membership figure of 60 million indicates a conversion rate to paid of roughly 14%, derived by the analyst; no country breakdown of members

claim: Patreon's own valuation collapsed roughly 70% from $4 billion in April 2021 to an internal mark of $1.5 billion, indicating that the platform economics underlying creator payouts deteriorated alongside the flattening of creator earnings.
stance_target: The claim that the creator-economy growth narrative diverged from measured platform and creator earnings after 2021
scope_conditions: Private company; valuation marks are reported via Crunchbase and Business Insider rather than disclosed; internal marks are not audited public valuations; total funding raised is $418.1 million across 11 rounds
quoted_support: Patreon's valuation reportedly stands at $1.5 billion (that's 70% drop from the last public valuation of $4 billion in 2021).

claim: Podcasting is Patreon's second-largest category with over 40,000 creators earning $472 million in 2024 from more than 6.7 million paid memberships, implying mean podcast-creator earnings of roughly $11,800 for the year and about $70 per paid membership annually.
stance_target: The claim about category-level earnings concentration within membership platforms
scope_conditions: Company-reported category figures from Patreon newsroom; the per-creator and per-membership figures are derived by the analyst and are means, not medians, over a category whose top ranks include creators earning $200,000+/month — so the median podcaster earns far less; 'over 40,000' is an imprecise denominator
quoted_support: In 2024, the earnings of podcasters on the Patreon platform reached $472 million from over 6.7 million paid memberships

claim: Graphtreon-derived Patreon statistics are structurally incomplete because creators can hide their earnings, so all published Patreon payout totals are visible-earnings subtotals of unknown coverage rather than platform telemetry.
stance_target: The claim that third-party Patreon earnings data constitutes complete platform telemetry
scope_conditions: Coverage gap is acknowledged by the source but never quantified; comparing Graphtreon's ~$24M/month visible payouts against Patreon's disclosed $2B/year (~$167M/month) implies visible earnings capture only about 14% of total payouts, derived by the analyst; this makes Graphtreon reliable for CREATOR COUNTS (which are visible for all creators with a paying member) but unreliable for earnings LEVELS
quoted_support: Creators on Patreon earned a total of $23.97 million (excluding creators with hidden earnings; actual earnings may vary significantly) in January 2026.

claim: This page is a Semrush-owned SEO content property whose Patreon revenue table contains a duplicated year label — listing 2022 twice and attributing the $228 million figure to 2022 in the table while the body text assigns it to 2024 — a data-hygiene error indicating the aggregator layer requires verification even when it cites real sources.
stance_target: The claim that well-sourced statistics aggregators transmit figures without error
scope_conditions: Error confined to the revenue table; the creator-count and payout tables cite Graphtreon consistently and are the load-bearing data on this page; the page discloses its ownership and that content is written by Semrush employees or paid contractors
quoted_support: | 2023 | $180-200 million | | 2022 | $228 million | ... Patreon generated an estimated revenue of $228 million in 2024.
